Painted still of an old Korean village well at hot noon, camera low at the rim. Round granite well rim, timber beam, hemp rope, grey giwa hall soft behind, gold millet in heat haze. The well is swollen and dripping wet: its dark round mouth brims and spills over the glistening lip in slow pulses, and from every crack between the fitted stones water spurts out in thin jets and trickles down in shining streams, soaking the dry packed earth into a dark wet pool. The thick hemp rope hangs slick and heavy into the mouth. A bucket on the beam has tipped and gushes. A ripe split apricot lies on the wet rim, juice running. Dusty-rose and dusty-gold #e8a04a light on the wet granite, a red #e8563f thread knotted on the rope. Helpless, aching, dripping arousal. PAINTED STILL — no people, no figures, no faces, no hands anywhere in the frame; the place or object IS the subject. Openly erotic metaphor: the shapes, wetness, swelling, thrusting and release unmistakably read as bodies and sex, the way a frank erotic painting does — yet everything stays landscape and object, no nudity, no literal anatomy. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). Hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL: granulated wet-in-wet washes and broken-colour dabs for sky, water and stone, dry-brush texture, soft bleeding edges and a faint paper grain; oil glazes deepen the darks and a touch of impasto lands on the single brightest highlight. Romantic-painting layout: one bold shape, at least half the frame quiet negative space, distant detail dissolving into haze. Film tenebrism: one hard directional key (sun, moon or lamp) against big dark masses, a thin edge of real light along the subject, painted bokeh from small real lights. Beautiful, luminous, painterly. NOT photoreal, NOT 3D, NOT a cartoon. No text. No watermark. DAY GROUND: the frame is built on WHITE — a high-key, paper-white ground: pale bright sky, white haze and mist, sunlit plaster and pale stone dissolving into bare white paper at the edges, the shadows few, crisp and cool-grey; the figure is the dark, inked thing in a bright frame. Never a black void, never a dim dusk wash.
